I went back to that place again this morning when I saw the tall tower
and the long archway still standing; but they had both changed since I
last saw them in childhood. The old house seemed almost to have become
a part of some wild forest--it was so full of ivy and so green with
the grass. The only thing that had remained unchanged was its roof,
which I climbed up on my hands, just as I did once before. And while
climbing it I noticed how very different the sky looked through the
roof to what it looks like all round the outside of the house now. It
is true that if one stands by the open door one can see the blue sky;
but then he is also looking out into a garden which has been planted by
children. But I stood on the roof and could look out directly into
some vast sea of heaven above me. There were no clouds there--no thin
veils upon the blue, nothing except the unbroken blue. I felt suddenly
as though I could climb up higher than any man ever has done, climbing
upwards until one came where the sun shone directly through pure air
into a world of fire.

........

The next day the whole thing collapsed, and I don’t know whether I shall
ever get used to its being gone. Perhaps I may find myself going there
again, perhaps for fun, or simply because of something else.
